relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with GAMT deficiency carrying a GAMT variant: 'Sanger sequencing of GAMT identified a novel homozygous variant c.235C>T'.
method_note: Letter-format case report of one unnamed boy; labelled 'patient' (rule 5; 'our patient' is a role word). Built by a short script from my reading; no tables in the paper. Age 'two year and five months old' (presentation) and '29-months-old' (introduction) agree; recorded the latter as age at report although follow-up continued at least nine months after therapy began, so it is effectively age at presentation; age at diagnosis not stated. Country/ethnicity not recorded: the paper only says there are few reports 'from the Indian subcontinent' without stating the patient's origin. Transcript printed is an Ensembl ID (ENST00000252288), recorded as printed. Variant type 'nonsense' taken from the authors' description 'premature stop codon'. Pathogenicity rests on in silico and population-frequency statements; no functional assay, so functional_evidence_statement is not reported. No parental testing reported. Normal findings recorded per D-27: nerve conduction, serum creatine kinase and serum creatinine 'were normal'; 'Tandem mass spectrometry revealed no abnormalities' is a whole investigation and is recorded as written, excluding nothing more specific. 'seizures and extrapyramidal signs were not observed' excludes seizures; the broader 'extrapyramidal signs' was recorded as excluded in phenotypic_features but not used to exclude the narrower checklist items dystonia, chorea or tremor (left not reported). Language delay was not taken as 'absent or limited speech'. The Author's Note says the case's MRI and the case were presented at conferences (RSNA 2017 poster, 2018 meetings); these are presentations, not cited publications, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients was left null. Post-treatment improvement included in treatment_summary. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: creatine monohydrate 500 mg/kg/d in three doses, low protein diet (0.5 gm/kg/d) to restrict arginine, and sodium benzoate; rapid improvement in socio-cognitive skills and near complete resolution of globus pallidi signal changes on follow-up imaging
span: Our patient was treated with creatine monohydrate at 500 mg/kg/d divided in three doses, low protein diet (0.5 gm/kg/d) to restrict arginine and also sodium benzoate
Rapid improvement in socio-cognitive skills was observed
follow-up imaging nine months after the initiation of therapy showed near complete resolution of signal changes in the globus pallidi and a presence of small creatine peak on MRS

disease_label_as_stated.span: most consistent with a diagnosis of GAMT-D

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: biochemical (elevated urinary guanidinoacetate) and genetic (Sanger sequencing of GAMT); MRS showed absent creatine peak
span: GAMT-D was diagnosed based on the elevated urinary excretion of guanidinoacetate (GAA), and identification of a novel pathogenic variant in GAMT
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) revealed an absence of creatine peak
urine testing showed increased excretion of GAA (1202 mmol/mol creatinine; normal < 200 mmol/mol creatinine), most consistent with a diagnosis of GAMT-D
Sanger sequencing of GAMT identified a novel homozygous variant c.235C>T
